Because Cart Abandoners account for only 3% of total traffic, capturing 100% of this segment would only raise conversion to 21.6%, leaving a shortfall of 2.12 percentage points and causing severe net contribution loss. Given that experimentation is scarce (1 experiment remaining, costing ~2.8x the annual profit pool), risking budget on a mathematically unviable offer is unjustified.

assessment.prediction: Waiving the Rs.30 shipping fee will lift overall conversion from 19.0% to at least 22.5%, generating positive net incremental contribution per customer after accounting for the Rs.30 shipping cost per order.
assessment.reasoning: Cart abandoners account for 40% of customers and explicitly drop off at checkout due to shipping fees, while Small-basket regulars (24%) report shipping thresholds as their primary purchase barrier. A past free-shipping trial successfully increased conversion, but contribution was never verified. At Rs.177 contribution per order after waiving Rs.30, conversion must reach 22.22% (+3.22% absolute lift) to break even. With 64% of customers friction-sensitive to shipping costs, achieving a +3.5% lift to 22.5% conversion is well within reach.

assessment.selection_rationale: Baseline contribution per customer is Rs.39.33 (19.0% * Rs.207). int_shipping lowers per-order contribution to Rs.177, requiring 22.22% conversion (+3.22% lift). int_pct (5% off) lowers contribution to Rs.168.15, requiring 23.39% conversion (+4.39% lift). int_flat (Rs.60 off) lowers contribution to Rs.147, requiring 26.75% conversion (+7.75% lift). int_bundle yields ~Rs.186.19 contribution requiring 21.12% conversion (+2.12% lift), but conflicts with Small-basket regulars who 'rarely bundles'. int_shipping is the most realistic to hit given exact segment motivations. int_shipping directly addresses the cited pain points of 64% of the customer base (Cart abandoners and Small-basket regulars) at a minimal cost of Rs.30 per order, offering the clearest path to exceeding its +3.22% break-even conversion threshold.

assessment.selection_rationale: Baseline contribution per visitor is Rs.78.47 (15.6% conversion * Rs.503 contribution/order). To break even: int_shipping (Rs.30 cost, Rs.473 contribution/order) requires 16.59% conversion (+0.99% absolute lift); int_bundle (+Rs.59 AOV, 2% discount, Rs.482.20 contribution/order) requires 16.27% conversion (+0.67% absolute lift); int_flat (Rs.50 discount, Rs.453 contribution/order) requires 17.32% conversion (+1.72% absolute lift); int_pct (7% off / Rs.126.70 discount, Rs.376.30 contribution/order) requires 20.85% conversion (+5.25% absolute lift). int_bundle has the lowest break-even threshold, followed closely by int_shipping. While int_bundle has a slightly lower absolute break-even threshold (+0.67% vs +0.99%), int_shipping directly addresses the explicit friction documented in customer support tickets (checkout abandonment over shipping fees). Testing int_shipping also rigorously resolves the merchant's unverified past trial, proving whether eliminating shipping friction delivers net contribution growth.

Unlike sitewide or flat discounts that reduce margin on existing single-item sales without expanding basket value, int_bundle increases top-line basket size by Rs.372, softening discount erosion and capitalizing on verified intent.

assessment.selection_rationale: int_shipping (Rs.80 discount) drops contribution per order to Rs.738, requiring a conversion lift from 15.3% to 16.96% (+1.66 pp). int_flat (Rs.140 discount) drops contribution to Rs.678, requiring conversion of 18.46% (+3.16 pp). int_pct (10% off / ~Rs.217) drops contribution to Rs.601, requiring conversion of 20.82% (+5.52 pp). int_bundle increases AOV to ~Rs.2,541, generating ~Rs.678 contribution per order post-discount; because it expands baseline basket size by Rs.372, it requires lower volume lift to generate positive incremental contribution compared to pure price cuts on single items. int_bundle is the only intervention supported by explicit organic customer feedback ('Requests to bundle two SKUs that customers already buy together') and structural basket expansion (+Rs.372 AOV). This combination protects contribution dollars per transaction far better than flat or percentage discounts on baseline order sizes.

assessment.reasoning: The conversion drift and falling AOV at Nutbox Labs are driven by operational friction and stockouts rather than price resistance. Customer service feedback points directly to damaged packaging on heavy SKUs and stockouts of popular lines. Crucially, the nearest competitor successfully raised prices by ~8% without losing share, demonstrating that customers in this category are quality- and availability-driven rather than discount-sensitive. Furthermore, 49% of the customer base (Bulk Regulars and Gift Buyers) are price-insensitive, meaning any broad discount or bundle intervention would heavily subsidize purchases that would have occurred at full price, destroying incremental contribution margin. Spending the merchant's single experiment budget on a promotional campaign under these conditions carries a negative expected value.
